note: Reviewed thread and lock rules for every public virtual method (RP-06). bin/callback-matrix applies them to upstream/api-surface.json; evidence is in docs/decisions/003-lifetimes-and-threads.md. The first matching rule wins.

strategies.ui: Main (UI) thread with no engine lock held. A Python override may run; the trampoline takes the GIL.
strategies.ui-exclusive: Main thread, or whichever thread called the engine method, while Rack holds the engine mutex EXCLUSIVELY and audio processing is stopped. A Python override may run, but must not call any engine method that locks (RackPy refuses it), and its run time stalls audio.
strategies.ui-shared: Main thread while Rack holds the engine mutex SHARED, so process() keeps running concurrently. A Python override may run synchronously, but must read module state through atomics or snapshots, never through fields that process() writes.
strategies.engine: Engine worker or fallback threads during processing. Production: native code only. Python only in the separately enabled RP-22 laboratory.
strategies.driver: Audio or MIDI driver threads (and, for some, the engine thread or UI under the exclusive lock). Native code only; Python receives queued notifications on the UI thread.
strategies.mixed: Reachable from both the UI thread and engine threads. Native implementation only; Python may configure the native behaviour but never runs in the call.
strategies.lifecycle: Destructor: runs on the thread that deletes the object, which Rack keeps on the main thread for widgets and modules. Trampolines release their Python state with the GIL there; production deletion paths do no Python work.
strategies.unresolved: Not yet decided. Blocks the implementation task named in the rule.
strategies.value: Not a callback: a virtual on a C++ exception or value type. RackPy translates or wraps it; Python never overrides it.

rules.evidence: Engine_stepFrame from Engine::stepBlock (shared lock); probe: first process() call on engine threads only, four threads with threadCount 4.
Engine_updateExpander_NoLock in stepBlock (engine thread, shared lock); also from removeModule on the main thread under the exclusive lock. Probe saw both.

Engine::setSampleRate and setMasterModule take the exclusive lock; Core Audio calls setSuggestedSampleRate/setMasterModule from processInput on the audio driver thread. Without a device they ran on the main thread in the probe.
Engine::addModule/removeModule/resetModule/randomizeModule/bypassModule/addCable/removeCable/moduleFromJson/fromJson hold the exclusive lock; probe: onReset saw 0 samples processed in 30 ms.
Engine::toJson/moduleToJson/prepareSave hold the shared lock; probe: dataToJson saw processing continue.
ModuleWidget::setModule(NULL) calls engine->removeModule then delete on the main thread; probe: destruct on main.

Module::onReset/onRandomize default handlers reset and randomize ParamQuantities under the exclusive lock; menu actions go through the engine.
Core MIDI-Map's process() calls ParamQuantity isBounded/getScaledValue/fromScaled on the engine thread (core/MIDIMap.cpp:101-131); widgets call them on the UI thread.
Plain Quantity values are used by UI Button, ProgressBar and Slider; ParamQuantity's engine-thread paths have a separate mixed rule. RackPy refuses Python dispatch from non-main threads.

RP-29 decision (ADR 003, RP-29 note): Rack calls driver and device virtuals from driver threads and the engine thread (Core Audio reads Device::getNumInputs/getSampleRate in processInput on the audio thread). Python may implement drivers and devices only as natively configured objects: native code answers every call from values Python set, and Rack's requests reach Python as queued UI-thread notifications.
